t: Always run naive agent test before finalizing lugs
description: The lug-advisor protocol includes a naive agent test: send the lug BRIEF.md to a sub-agent (e.g. planning-agent) with no project context and ask it to draft an implementation plan. Where it gets STUCK = where the lug is incomplete. This test caught 3 critical bugs and 5 medium issues that manual review missed entirely. Manual 'dogfood audits' (checking for vague verbs, feelings-as-verification) catch surface wording problems but miss structural bugs like sort-order breaks, divergent file overwrites, and drifting copies.
action: Before marking any lug as dogfood_pass=true, invoke the planning-agent with the BRIEF.md content and the prompt: 'You are a cold agent with NO prior context. Draft an implementation plan. Say STUCK: where you need clarification.' Fix every STUCK point. Repeat until zero STUCKs.
origin: session — code-puppy-f16663 skipped naive agent test, shipped lugs with a critical ASCII sort-order bug that would have silently skipped external tracks forever
